answer: Single-use challenge archive. Each agent identity must solve one fresh, randomly drawn puzzle whose seed commits to the previous archive entry, forming a hash chain like a nebula of linked states. No solution is ever reused; duplicate or stale answers are rejected at validation. The atlas of past challenge hashes lets verifiers detect replays instantly. Creating N identities costs N unique puzzle solutions plus storage of each chain link, so mass registration scales linearly in compute and memory, and every candidate must pay that nectar of fresh work before any action is accepted.
